column3: “Be subject” is rendered “be submissive,” and “conduct” “behavior”; NASB follows the critical text (“they may be won”).
“In fear pure conduct” is rendered “chaste and respectful behavior.”
NASB supplies “adornment,” “merely,” and “jewelry”; “garments” is rendered “dresses.”
NASB supplies “let it be” and “quality”; “of great worth” is rendered “precious.”
NASB follows the critical text (“hoped in God”); “being subject” is rendered “being submissive.”
NASB supplies “her” and “if”; “not fearing any consternation” is rendered “without being frightened by any fear.”
“According to knowledge” is rendered “in an understanding way”; NASB supplies “your wives” and renders “joint-heirs” as the singular “a fellow heir,” applying it to the wife.
NASB follows the critical text (“humble in spirit”); “the end” is rendered “To sum up.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “knowing”; it adds “very purpose.”
The quotation is in capitals.
NASB follows the critical text (“turn away”).
NASB supplies “attend.”
NASB follows the critical text (“zealous”); “shall be” is rendered “prove.”
“Threats” is rendered “intimidation.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Christ as Lord”); it moves “yet with gentleness and reverence” into this verse.
NASB follows the critical text, without “as of evildoers”; “conduct” is rendered “behavior.”
NASB restructures the comparison.
NASB has “died,” where the critical text has “suffered”; it reads “us” with the Textus Receptus, where the critical text has “you.”
“Preached” is rendered “made proclamation”; NASB adds “now.”
“Souls” is rendered “persons,” and “saved” “brought safely”; NASB follows the critical text (“kept waiting”).
NASB follows the critical text (“saves you”); “demand” is rendered “an appeal,” and “filth” “dirt.”
Close to the Greek.
